summary: Ran M3-S04's molecular tests from the build directory. XML: 1 of 1 *-meta.xml file (discountApprovalPanel.js-meta.xml) parsed. Manifest: skipped-not-applicable, naming M4-S04 as the step that carries the LightningComponentBundle member - this step is lwc-builder/ui, not the apex-builder/automation case build-orchestration.md Section 5 literally names, so this is a documented extension by analogy (per operator instruction and the M3-S03 tester's precedent), not a literal instance of the Apex exception; see Process Observations. The one declared checker, check_lwc_base_component_recipes.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M3-S04, ran verbatim from the build directory and exited 0 ('1 bundle(s), 0 loose template(s) scanned - 0 ERROR, 0 WARN'), reproducing lwc-builder's own reported result exactly. check-outputs confirmed ok:true and artefact_hashes were recorded for all 4 declared outputs. No command-type acceptance test is declared, and in particular no declared test runs Jest - confirmed by reading plan.json's acceptance_tests[] directly, all 5 entries are checker/xml/manifest/manual/manual. Independently verified Jest could not run here regardless: no package.json, node_modules or sfdx-lwc-jest anywhere from the repo root up to /Users/pranavnagrecha, and `npx --no-install sfdx-lwc-jest --version` fails ('could not determine executable to run'). node --check was not run and was not substituted as a parse check, since LWC modules use decorators and ESM that node --check cannot evaluate. Two manual acceptance tests are deferred to the M3 milestone gate, never ticked here; both are Given/When/Then-shaped with an observable outcome, so neither is unusable. Both were spot-checked against the artefacts as due diligence: manual line 2 (discountThreshold default 20, description naming Opportunity_Discount_Requires_Approval, supportedFormFactors Large+Small, target lightning__RecordPage scoped to Opportunity) matches discountApprovalPanel.js-meta.xml exactly. Manual line 1's four named button-disabled assertions (20-null-disabled, 25-null-enabled, 25-Pending-disabled, 25-Approved-disabled) are all verbatim present in the test file, but the same describe block actually holds 7 button-state cases, not 4 - the line's count undercounts the file, though the four it names are correct. results.json passed:true (failed[] empty), so the step was moved built -> tested via set-status.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual (Step 7 HIGH row): both always-on checks completed, the one declared checker's exit code was observed directly by this agent, check-outputs reported ok:true with no missing/empty/malformed outputs, and no command-type test was declared to be refused. None of the three literal Step 7 MEDIUM triggers fired: no command test was refused, no metadata-api-coverage-gaps exclusion was applied, and check-outputs was clean. The manifest disposition rests on an analogy the plan's own acceptance_tests[2].description pre-committed to at authoring time and that the operator's instruction and the M3-S03 tester's precedent both confirm, rather than on an incomplete artifact - kept HIGH on that basis, with the literal-text gap flagged under Process Observations rather than folded silently into the pass.

standards/build-orchestration.md Section 5's manifest carve-out ('The Apex exception') literally names only an apex-builder-owned automation step; M3-S04 is lwc-builder/ui, so the always-on manifest rule's plain text would have this step's type-based fail branch apply once a package.xml is confirmed absent from its own artefacts. A package.xml DOES exist under a depends_on step (M1-S01's), which if read literally under AGENT.md Step 3 rule 1 would mean the check does not even reach the type-fail branch - it would instead run file-to-manifest against M1-S01's package.xml (StandardValueSet, BusinessProcess, RecordType, CustomField members only) and fail on the bundle's derived LightningComponentBundle member having no covering entry. Neither literal path was taken; per operator instruction, this step's manifest check was treated identically to M3-S03's Apex exception - skipped-not-applicable, naming M4-S04 - matching this step's own acceptance_tests[2].description, which pre-committed to that reading at plan-authoring time by direct analogy to Section 4's borrowed-agent condition 2 (lwc-builder's Output Contract names no package.xml, so it cannot declare one). Recommend formalizing a second named carve-out in Section 5 - a 'borrowed-agent output-contract exception' generalizing the Apex one to any step whose owning agent's Output Contract produces no manifest - so a future tester does not need an operator instruction or a prior-step precedent to resolve the same gap on M3-S05 or any other non-Apex, no-manifest step type.
